thread.title: South Korea Stock Market May Extend Winning Streak

author: rttnews.com
title: South Korea Stock Market May Extend Winning Streak
text:
The South Korea stock market has moved higher in consecutive trading days, gathering almost 30 points or 1.4 percent along the way. The KOSPI now rests just above the 2,205-point plateau and it's expected to add to its winnings on Thursday.
The global forecast for the Asian markets is broadly positive on an improved outlook for interest rates and a spike in crude oil prices. The European and U.S. markets were up and the Asian bourses are predicted to follow suit.
The KOSPI finished sharply higher on Wednesday following gains from the steel companies technology stocks and financial shares.
For the day, the index climbed 22.84 points or 1.05 percent to finish at the daily high of 2,206.20 after moving as low as 2,177.88. Volume was 469 million shares worth 6.77 trillion won. There were 501 gainers and 329 decliners.
Among the actives, Shinhan Financial collected 0.83 percent, while KB Financial climbed 1.19 percent, Hana Financial rose 0.26 percent, Samsung Electronics spiked 1.98 percent, LG Electronics added 0.30 percent, LG Display tumbled 3.66 percent, SK hynix soared 3.41 percent, SK Telecom plunged 3.36 percent, KEPCO perked 0.76 percent, S-Oil gained 0.49 percent, POSCO surged 6.15 percent and Hyundai Steel jumped 1.58 percent.
The lead from Wall Street is firm in response to the Federal Reserve's monetary policy announcement, which sent the major averages to nearly two-month closing highs.
The Dow added 434.90 points or 1.77 while the NASDAQ surged 154.79 points or 2.20 rose 41.05 points or 1.55 percent to 2,681.05.
Stocks accelerated to the upside after the Fed
Positive sentiment was also generated by solid earnings news from companies like Boeing (BA) and Apple (AAPL).
 West Texas Intermediate Crude oil futures barrel.
Closer to home, South Korea will see December numbers for industrial production and retail sales later this morning. In November, industrial production was down 1.7 percent on month and up 0.1 percent on year, while retail sales added 0.5 percent on month and 1.0 percent on year.
